findings.claim: A run the record says is still executing is painted as a terminal failure:env — the same lie as the spinner, pointed the other way, and worse because the run's real result is then never shown.
findings.evidence: src/browser/server.py es.onerror else-branch called lost(), which sets #progress[data-terminal]=failure and the failure colour. A proxy idle timeout or sleeping laptop over a live run is the ordinary case; stream_task's gen() has no keepalive.
findings.repro: a fourth submit({status:'running'}) in the case harness: terminal 'failure', status_class 'big failure'.
findings.acceptance: no verdict, no data-terminal, no spinner, buttons released; run id kept on screen.

findings.claim: The browser check's stream keeps its own handle and its own onerror, so the exact spinner-over-a-dead-run defect stayed open on the button beside the fixed one.
findings.evidence: src/browser/server.py — s is a const local inside smoke(); busy() closed only es; s.onerror did not reach a terminal state.
findings.repro: drive smoke() with an EventSource that errors: #status 'running', animationName 'spin', no data-terminal.
findings.acceptance: same treatment as the task stream; busy() owns both handles.

findings.claim: The stale-poll assertion is vacuous — deleting both cross-run guards keeps the case green.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py let the poll land before reassigning runId, then compared #status with itself (both sides 'stream lost').
findings.repro: delete the runId!==mine guards and run the case — passes.
findings.acceptance: hold the poll open across the reassignment; assert the old record never reaches #result and its screenshots never reach #pvshot.

findings.claim: SEM.locked() is a read, not an acquire, so two browser checks still launch two Chromiums and /readyz reports neither.
findings.evidence: src/browser/server.py smoke_events early return; /readyz reads SEM.locked() too.
findings.acceptance: T-M40-1: the smoke path takes the same semaphore, pinned by a case.

findings.claim: The new case's restore block leaks runId, #status, #progress state and an unremovable unhandledrejection listener into the shared _ui_page render; inert today only by luck of case ordering.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py restore block; ui-rendered-narrow happens to call resetProgress() first and happens to omit screenshot from its step payload.
findings.repro: add a screenshot key to ui-rendered-narrow's payload.
findings.acceptance: restore everything the case touched, and name the listener so it can be removed.
